# Package architecture, source reports, and reproduction {#sec-reference}

## Relationship to the `medusa` R Package

This Quarto book lives in the `book/` directory of the standalone `medusa` R package (`0.1.0`, excluded from CRAN/tarball builds via `.Rbuildignore`). Every simulation, figure, and diagnostic table in the active chapters was executed directly against `library(medusa)`—incorporating the complete modern pipeline architecture:

| Pipeline component | Core `medusa` functions | Key methodological features |
|:---|:---|:---|
| **Step 1 · NIfTI matrix I/O, HRF & AR($p$) noise** | `read_nifti_ts()`, `hrf_library()`, `estimate_crossrun_hrf()` | Streaming C++ 4D NIfTI ↔ `T × V` matrix extraction with pre-flight geometry checks, 3D physiological HRF manifold (`preset = "medusa"`), out-of-sample cross-run evidence pooling, 2-pass target-excluding REML AR($p$) noise refit, Winsorized GLS marginal `noise_sd`, and task-free `noise_innovations`. |
| **Step 2 · Event-informed continuous deconvolution** | `deconvolve_crossrun_hrf()`, `diagnose_crossrun_recovery()`, `write_nifti_ts()`, `deconvolve_reglin()`, `deconvolve_nlreg()` | Continuous neural source recovery with event-supported `lambda` tuning, adaptive kurtosis/tail-triggered `rwls = "auto"` glitch downweighting, `"noise_sd"` scaling, explicit `hrf_inverse_operator()` strata, and streaming C++ 3D/4D NIfTI export (`deconvolve_nlreg()` retained as blind Bush & Cisler 2011 comparator). |
| **Step 3 · Trial-epoch readout, alignment & demixing** | `decon_epoch_regression()`, `align_medusa_ts()`, `evt_align_decon_files()` | Kernel quadrature onto peri-event lag grids, collateral non-target removal (`demix_other_events`), post-readout ridge target demixing (`demix_target_trials`), within-trial lag demixing (`demix_within_trial`), duration `"rate"` vs. `"integral"` readout, exact Toeplitz error propagation (`se_demixed`), and fast C++ matrix-native descriptive alignment (`align_medusa_ts()`). |
| **Step 4 · Parcel panels & cohort weights** | `decon_epoch_regression(..., parcel_groups = ...)` | Multi-stratum inverse-variance parcel pooling using task-free `noise_innovations`, `shared_noise_loading` & `unit_error_cor` export, `precision_weight` & `precision_weight_cohort`, and matched ZCA panel whitening (`whiten_panel`). |
| **Step 5 · Group & trajectory inference** | `mixed_by()`, `medusa_multilag_infer()`, `backproject_medusa()` | Cohort-weighted split-wise REML mixed models (`lmerTest`), joint multi-lag trajectories with available-case pooling, spectral deblurring, Marra–Wood P-splines, studentized Wishart `Max-|T|` / 1D TFCE / omnibus tests, `"unsmoothed"` window contrasts, and streaming NIfTI map backprojection. |
| **Step 6 · Trial connectivity & PPI** | `decon_connectivity_repair()`, `medusa_fit_mmom()`, `medusa_between_subject_repair()` | Within-trial M-MOMS predictor disattenuation, automatic cross-parcel `shared_error = "auto"` subtraction, exact residualized-seed covariance projection, and HKSJ random-effects participant pooling. |

For NIfTI matrix and file-backed workflows (`read_nifti_ts()`, `write_nifti_ts()`, `align_medusa_ts()`, `voxelwise_deconvolution()`, and `evt_align_decon_files()`), see the package vignettes (`vignettes/medusa-workflows.Rmd` and `vignettes/medusa-docs.md`) and function reference (`?read_nifti_ts`, `?estimate_crossrun_hrf`, `?deconvolve_crossrun_hrf`, `?align_medusa_ts`, `?decon_epoch_regression`, `?medusa_multilag_infer`, `?decon_connectivity_repair`).

## Reproducing All Simulations, Figures, and the Book

With `medusa` and its plotting/reporting dependencies (`ggplot2`, `data.table`, `lmerTest`, `knitr`, `rmarkdown`) installed in R, render the book from `book/`:

```bash
quarto render
```

Because `quarto render` reads the saved `.rds` and `.csv` outputs generated by each chapter's standalone scripts, rendering completes in seconds. To regenerate every simulation, diagnostic table, and figure from scratch against the installed `medusa` package, run the chapter scripts below from `book/`:

<details>
<summary>Show full simulation and figure regeneration commands</summary>

```bash
# Conceptual forward-model schematic
Rscript assets/forward-model.R

# End-to-end worked example & M-MOM covariance verification
(cd worked && Rscript run.R && Rscript mmom-check.R && Rscript checkpoints.R)

# Step 1: Cross-run HRF & AR(p) noise + Woolrich noise review
(cd medusa_step1_hrf_noise && Rscript simulate_step1.R && Rscript figures_step1.R)
(cd medusa_step1_hrf_noise/woolrich_review && Rscript compare_noise.R && Rscript variance_check.R && Rscript plot_comparison.R)

# Step 2: Event-informed continuous deconvolution (including blind vs. event-informed benchmark)
(cd medusa_step2_deconvolution && Rscript simulate_step2.R && Rscript figures_step2.R)

# Step 3: Peri-event epoch readout & demixing
(cd medusa_step3_epochs && Rscript simulate_step3.R && Rscript figures_step3.R)

# Step 4: Parcel aggregation, shared noise loadings, & cohort precision weights
(cd medusa_step4_parcel_panels && Rscript simulate_step4.R && Rscript figures_step4.R)

# Step 5: Split-wise mixed models & joint multi-lag trajectory inference
(cd medusa_step5_group_models && Rscript simulate_step5.R && Rscript figures_step5.R && Rscript simulate_pr62.R && Rscript figures_pr62.R)

# Multi-lag trajectory empirical calibration (180 replications x 2 regimes)
(cd medusa_pr62_calibration && Rscript simulate.R && Rscript figures.R)

# Step 6: Trial-level connectivity, M-MOMS, & PPI sensitivity
(cd medusa_step6_connectivity && Rscript simulate.R && Rscript figures.R)
(cd medusa_connectivity_inference && Rscript prepare_figures.R)

# Render full Quarto HTML book to _book/
quarto render
```

</details>

## Key Methodological References

- Bush, K., & Cisler, J. (2013). Decoding neural events from fMRI BOLD signal: a comparison of existing methods and development of a new fast method. *Magnetic Resonance Imaging*, 31(6), 976–989.
- Woolrich, M. W., Ripley, B. D., Brady, M., & Smith, S. M. (2001). Temporal autocorrelation in univariate linear modeling of FMRI data. *NeuroImage*, 14(6), 1370–1386. [DOI](https://doi.org/10.1006/nimg.2001.0931)
- Abdulrahman, H., & Henson, R. N. (2016). Effect of trial-to-trial variability on optimal event-related fMRI design. *NeuroImage*, 125, 756–766. [Article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4692520/)
- Marra, G., & Wood, S. N. (2012). Coverage properties of confidence intervals for generalized additive model components. *Scandinavian Journal of Statistics*, 39(1), 53–74.
- Kuznetsova, A., Brockhoff, P. B., & Christensen, R. H. B. (2017). `lmerTest` package: tests in linear mixed effects models. *Journal of Statistical Software*, 82(13), 1–26. [Article](https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v082i13)
- Benjamini, Y., & Yekutieli, D. (2001). The control of the false discovery rate in multiple testing under dependency. *Annals of Statistics*, 29(4), 1165–1188. [Article](https://doi.org/10.1214/aos/1013699998)
- Cole, M. W., Ito, T., Schultz, D., Mill, R., Chen, R., & Cocuzza, C. (2019). Task activations produce spurious but systematic inflation of task functional connectivity estimates. *NeuroImage*, 189, 1–18. [Article](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6422749/)
